descriptionChirho: The ordinal number fourth, indicating position in a sequence. Nine occurrences across multiple genders and cases (GFS, NNS, AFS, GNS, NMS, DFS) all describe the fourth item in a series—the fourth seal, fourth angel, fourth watch, etc. Translations are uniformly ordinal: Spanish 'cuarto/cuarta,' Hindi 'chauthe/chauthene,' Arabic 'ar-rabiʿ,' Korean 'netjjae,' Swahili 'wa-nne/ya-nne.' This sense is distinct from the fractional sense because every occurrence modifies a noun to mark sequential position rather than expressing a fraction or portion.

A fractional use meaning one-quarter or a fourth portion of something. The single occurrence (Rev 6:8, 'authority over a fourth of the earth') uses the accusative neuter singular to express a fraction rather than ordinal position. The multilingual evidence clearly distinguishes this from the ordinal sense: Spanish 'cuarta-parte' (lit. fourth-part), Hindi 'chauthai' (fractional form distinct from ordinal 'chauthe'), Arabic 'rubʿi' (the standard fraction word, not the ordinal 'rabiʿ'), Korean 'sabun-ui-il' (one-fourth), Swahili 'robo' (quarter, not the ordinal 'nne'). Every target language uses a distinct lexical form for the fraction vs the ordinal.
